It exhibits the parity and copy witnesses (showing that the conditional and unconditional readings are logically independent, one being 0 while the other is 1 bit, and conversely); confirms over hundreds of random populations and random merges that a merge never raises the conditional reading; verifies the exact loss identity by comparing the measured drop against the sum of its per-(context, fiber) contributions; verifies the two-sided audit bracket and demonstrates exactness without injectivity; confirms the chain rule I(X;Y|Z) = I(X;(Y,Z)) - I(X;Z) on arbitrary nonnegative weights; verifies that merges compose and that readings decay monotonically along a chain; exhibits the product-block dichotomy by breaking proportionality in a single cell; demonstrates that context merges are two-sided by both destroying and manufacturing a full bit of dependence; and checks the capacity cap I(X;Y|Z) <= H(X|Z). Every check is an assertion, so the script fails loudly if any identity were to break.
demos.code:
"""
One-Sidedness of Conditional-Independence Artifacts
===================================================

Numerical companion to the paper.  Everything is self-contained: the entropy
functional, the fiber deficit, mutual information, conditional mutual
information, label merges, and every theorem-level identity is recomputed
numerically on explicit tables.

Conventions
-----------
*   A *weight* is an arbitrary nonnegative function on a finite product set.
    Nothing is normalised: total mass may be any nonnegative number.
*   All logarithms are base 2, so all quantities are in bits.
*   `nlp(w) = -w log2 w`, with `nlp(0) = 0`.
*   `H(w) = sum_x nlp(w(x))`.
*   `D(S, w) = H(w restricted to S) - nlp(sum_{x in S} w(x))`  (the *fiber
    deficit*: the entropy inside the block that is destroyed by pooling it).
*   `MI(q) = H(q_X) + H(q_Y) - H(q)` for a weight `q` on `X x Y`.
*   `CMI(p) = sum_z [ MI(p_z) - nlp(mass(p_z)) ]` for a weight `p` on
    `X x Y x Z`, where `p_z` is the `z`-slice.

Run with:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
import random
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Cell3 = Tuple[Hashable, Hashable, Hashable]
Cell2 = Tuple[Hashable, Hashable]
Table3 = Dict[Cell3, float]
Table2 = Dict[Cell2, float]

TOL = 1e-9


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core information-theoretic functionals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def nlp(w: float) -> float:
    """The Shannon term -w log2 w, extended by nlp(0) = 0."""
    if w <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return -w * math.log2(w)


def entropy(values: Iterable[float]) -> float:
    """H(w) = sum of Shannon terms.  No normalisation is assumed."""
    return sum(nlp(v) for v in values)


def deficit(values: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Fiber deficit D(S, w) = H(w|_S) - nlp(sum_S w).

    This is the entropy that is destroyed when the block S is pooled into a
    single label.  It is nonnegative (Gibbs), and zero exactly when at most one
    element of the block carries mass.
    """
    return entropy(values) - nlp(sum(values))


def marg1(q: Table2, xs: Sequence[Hashable], ys: Sequence[Hashable]) -> Dict[Hashable, float]:
    """Row sums of a two-way table: q_X(x) = sum_y q(x, y)."""
    return {x: sum(q.get((x, y), 0.0) for y in ys) for x in xs}


def marg2(q: Table2, xs: Sequence[Hashable], ys: Sequence[Hashable]) -> Dict[Hashable, float]:
    """Column sums of a two-way table: q_Y(y) = sum_x q(x, y)."""
    return {y: sum(q.get((x, y), 0.0) for x in xs) for y in ys}


def mass(q: Table2) -> float:
    """Total mass of a two-way table."""
    return sum(q.values())


def MI(q: Table2, xs: Sequence[Hashable], ys: Sequence[Hashable]) -> float:
    """Unnormalised mutual information MI(q) = H(q_X) + H(q_Y) - H(q)."""
    return (
        entropy(marg1(q, xs, ys).values())
        + entropy(marg2(q, xs, ys).values())
        - entropy(q.get((x, y), 0.0) for x in xs for y in ys)
    )


def slice_at(p: Table3, z: Hashable) -> Table2:
    """The z-slice of a three-way table."""
    return {(x, y): v for (x, y, zz), v in p.items() if zz == z}


def CMI(
    p: Table3,
    xs: Sequence[Hashable],
    ys: Sequence[Hashable],
    zs: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> float:
    """Conditional mutual information I(X;Y|Z), summed slice by slice.

    For each context z we take the slice reading MI(p_z) and subtract the
    Shannon term of the slice mass; for a probability table this reduces to the
    textbook  sum p(x,y,z) log2 [ p(x,y,z) p(z) / (p(x,z) p(y,z)) ].
    """
    total = 0.0
    for z in zs:
        s = slice_at(p, z)
        total += MI(s, xs, ys) - nlp(mass(s))
    return total


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Label merges
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def fiber(f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable], u: Hashable, xs: Sequence[Hashable]) -> List[Hashable]:
    """The fiber f^{-1}(u) inside the dial alphabet xs."""
    return [x for x in xs if f(x) == u]


def push_fst3(
    f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    p: Table3,
    xs: Sequence[Hashable],
    ys: Sequence[Hashable],
    zs: Sequence[Hashable],
    us: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> Table3:
    """Merge the dial alphabet: (f_* p)(u, y, z) = sum_{x in f^{-1}(u)} p(x,y,z)."""
    out: Table3 = {}
    for u in us:
        fib = fiber(f, u, xs)
        for y in ys:
            for z in zs:
                out[(u, y, z)] = sum(p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for x in fib)
    return out


def push_thd(
    f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    p: Table3,
    xs: Sequence[Hashable],
    ys: Sequence[Hashable],
    zs: Sequence[Hashable],
    ws: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> Table3:
    """Merge the *context* alphabet.  No one-sidedness holds for this."""
    out: Table3 = {}
    for x in xs:
        for y in ys:
            for w in ws:
                out[(x, y, w)] = sum(p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for z in zs if f(z) == w)
    return out


def label_loss(
    f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    p: Table3,
    xs: Sequence[Hashable],
    ys: Sequence[Hashable],
    z: Hashable,
    us: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> float:
    """Label entropy destroyed by f inside the context z.

    labelLoss(z) = H(dial marginal in context z) - H(merged dial marginal).
    Only the *marginal* dial counts are needed, so an auditor can compute this
    without ever seeing the joint table.
    """
    s = slice_at(p, z)
    m1 = marg1(s, xs, ys)
    merged = {u: sum(m1[x] for x in fiber(f, u, xs)) for u in us}
    return entropy(m1.values()) - entropy(merged.values())


def marg_xz(
    p: Table3, xs: Sequence[Hashable], ys: Sequence[Hashable], zs: Sequence[Hashable]
) -> Table2:
    """The context channel table: (x, z) |-> sum_y p(x, y, z)."""
    return {(x, z): sum(p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in ys) for x in xs for z in zs}


def as_pair_table(
    p: Table3, xs: Sequence[Hashable], ys: Sequence[Hashable], zs: Sequence[Hashable]
) -> Table2:
    """Read a three-way table as the two-way table of X against the pair (Y,Z)."""
    return {(x, (y, z)): p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for x in xs for y in ys for z in zs}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Example populations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

BOOLS: List[Hashable] = [False, True]


def xor_population() -> Table3:
    """Uniform weight 1/4 on the four cells with z = x XOR y."""
    return {
        (x, y, z): (0.25 if ((x != y) == z) else 0.0)
        for x in BOOLS
        for y in BOOLS
        for z in BOOLS
    }


def copy_population() -> Table3:
    """Uniform weight 1/2 on the two cells with x = y = z."""
    return {
        (x, y, z): (0.5 if (x == y == z) else 0.0)
        for x in BOOLS
        for y in BOOLS
        for z in BOOLS
    }


def random_population(
    nx: int, ny: int, nz: int, rng: random.Random, sparsity: float = 0.25
) -> Table3:
    """A random nonnegative (unnormalised) weight on an nx x ny x nz grid."""
    p: Table3 = {}
    for x in range(nx):
        for y in range(ny):
            for z in range(nz):
                p[(x, y, z)] = 0.0 if rng.random() < sparsity else rng.random()
    return p


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Checks corresponding to the theorems
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def check(name: str, ok: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:
    flag = "OK  " if ok else "FAIL"
    print(f"  [{flag}] {name}" + (f"   {detail}" if detail else ""))
    if not ok:
        raise AssertionError(name)


def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 74)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 74)


def demo_witnesses() -> None:
    banner("1.  Two witness populations on {0,1}^3")

    xs = ys = zs = BOOLS
    xor = xor_population()
    cop = copy_population()

    xor_cmi = CMI(xor, xs, ys, zs)
    xor_single = MI({(x, y): sum(xor[(x, y, z)] for z in zs) for x in xs for y in ys}, xs, ys)
    cop_cmi = CMI(cop, xs, ys, zs)
    cop_single = MI({(x, y): sum(cop[(x, y, z)] for z in zs) for x in xs for y in ys}, xs, ys)

    print(f"  XOR population :  I(X;Y) = {xor_single:.6f} bits,  I(X;Y|Z) = {xor_cmi:.6f} bits")
    print(f"  copy population:  I(X;Y) = {cop_single:.6f} bits,  I(X;Y|Z) = {cop_cmi:.6f} bits")

    check("XOR: single-dial reading is 0", abs(xor_single) < TOL)
    check("XOR: conditional reading is 1 bit", abs(xor_cmi - 1.0) < TOL)
    check("copy: single-dial reading is 1 bit", abs(cop_single - 1.0) < TOL)
    check("copy: conditional reading is 0", abs(cop_cmi) < TOL)
    print("  => conditional and single-dial readings are logically independent:")
    print("     neither one bounds the other.")

    merge_all: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda _: True
    merged = push_fst3(merge_all, xor, xs, ys, zs, [True])
    merged_cmi = CMI(merged, [True], ys, zs)
    print(f"\n  Collapsing merge f(x) = * applied to XOR:  reading = {merged_cmi:.6f} bits")
    check("a reported conditional independence can be a pure artifact",
          abs(merged_cmi) < TOL and xor_cmi > TOL)

    total_label_loss = sum(label_loss(merge_all, xor, xs, ys, z, [True]) for z in zs)
    print(f"  observable label-entropy loss           = {total_label_loss:.6f} bits")
    check("error bar is attained exactly on this witness",
          abs((xor_cmi - merged_cmi) - total_label_loss) < TOL)


def demo_one_sidedness(trials: int = 400) -> None:
    banner("2.  One-sidedness: a dial merge never inflates the reading")

    rng = random.Random(20240908)
    xs = list(range(4))
    ys = list(range(3))
    zs = list(range(3))
    us = list(range(2))

    worst_violation = 0.0
    strict_drops = 0
    for _ in range(trials):
        p = random_population(len(xs), len(ys), len(zs), rng)
        # a random merge of the 4 dial settings onto 2 labels
        table = {x: rng.choice(us) for x in xs}
        f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda x, t=table: t[x]
        true_reading = CMI(p, xs, ys, zs)
        merged_reading = CMI(push_fst3(f, p, xs, ys, zs, us), us, ys, zs)
        worst_violation = max(worst_violation, merged_reading - true_reading)
        if merged_reading < true_reading - TOL:
            strict_drops += 1

    print(f"  {trials} random populations and random merges.")
    print(f"  largest observed value of  I(f(X);Y|Z) - I(X;Y|Z)  =  {worst_violation:.3e}")
    print(f"  strictly lowered readings: {strict_drops}/{trials}")
    check("no merge ever raised the conditional reading", worst_violation < TOL)


def demo_exact_accounting(trials: int = 200) -> None:
    banner("3.  Exact accounting: where the lost bits went")

    rng = random.Random(11235)
    xs = list(range(4))
    ys = list(range(3))
    zs = list(range(2))
    us = list(range(2))

    worst = 0.0
    sample_printed = False
    for _ in range(trials):
        p = random_population(len(xs), len(ys), len(zs), rng)
        table = {x: rng.choice(us) for x in xs}
        f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda x, t=table: t[x]

        loss = CMI(p, xs, ys, zs) - CMI(push_fst3(f, p, xs, ys, zs, us), us, ys, zs)

        localised = 0.0
        contributions: List[Tuple[Hashable, Hashable, float]] = []
        for z in zs:
            s = slice_at(p, z)
            m1 = marg1(s, xs, ys)
            for u in us:
                fib = fiber(f, u, xs)
                marg_def = deficit([m1[x] for x in fib])
                sliced_def = sum(deficit([s.get((x, y), 0.0) for x in fib]) for y in ys)
                contributions.append((z, u, marg_def - sliced_def))
                localised += marg_def - sliced_def

        worst = max(worst, abs(loss - localised))
        if not sample_printed:
            sample_printed = True
            print("  A single example, broken down by (context, fiber):")
            for z, u, c in contributions:
                print(f"    context z={z}, fiber f^-1({u}):  contributes {c:.6f} bits of loss")
            print(f"    total localised loss = {localised:.6f} bits")
            print(f"    actual drop in the reading = {loss:.6f} bits")

    print(f"\n  Over {trials} random instances, worst mismatch between the drop and the")
    print(f"  sum of its (context, fiber) contributions: {worst:.3e}")
    check("exact loss identity holds", worst < 1e-8)


def demo_error_bar(trials: int = 200) -> None:
    banner("4.  The observable error bar")

    rng = random.Random(31415)
    xs = list(range(5))
    ys = list(range(3))
    zs = list(range(2))
    us = list(range(3))

    slack: List[float] = []
    for _ in range(trials):
        p = random_population(len(xs), len(ys), len(zs), rng)
        table = {x: rng.choice(us) for x in xs}
        f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda x, t=table: t[x]
        loss = CMI(p, xs, ys, zs) - CMI(push_fst3(f, p, xs, ys, zs, us), us, ys, zs)
        bar = sum(label_loss(f, p, xs, ys, z, us) for z in zs)
        check_ok = -TOL <= loss <= bar + TOL
        if not check_ok:
            raise AssertionError("error bar violated")
        slack.append(bar - loss)

    print(f"  {trials} random instances; in every one")
    print("      0 <= I(X;Y|Z) - I(f(X);Y|Z) <= (label entropy destroyed by f).")
    print(f"  mean slack in the upper bound: {sum(slack) / len(slack):.6f} bits")
    print(f"  minimum slack observed:        {min(slack):.6f} bits")

    # exactness without injectivity: merge two dial settings that never co-occur
    p: Table3 = {}
    for x in xs:
        for y in ys:
            for z in zs:
                p[(x, y, z)] = 0.0
    #  dial 0 only ever fires in context 0, dial 1 only in context 1,
    #  so the merge {0,1} -> 0 destroys no label entropy in either context,
    #  while dials 2 and 3 keep the reading strictly positive.
    p[(0, 0, 0)] = 0.30
    p[(0, 1, 0)] = 0.10
    p[(2, 0, 0)] = 0.10
    p[(2, 1, 0)] = 0.30
    p[(3, 0, 0)] = 0.20
    p[(3, 1, 0)] = 0.05
    p[(1, 0, 1)] = 0.20
    p[(1, 2, 1)] = 0.40
    coll = {0: 0, 1: 0, 2: 1, 3: 2, 4: 3}
    collide: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda x, t=coll: t[x]
    lhs = CMI(push_fst3(collide, p, xs, ys, zs, [0, 1, 2, 3]), [0, 1, 2, 3], ys, zs)
    rhs = CMI(p, xs, ys, zs)
    print("\n  Exactness without injectivity: merging two settings that never occur")
    print("  in the same context leaves the reading untouched.")
    print(f"      merged reading = {lhs:.6f}   true reading = {rhs:.6f}")
    check("no label entropy destroyed => exact reading", abs(lhs - rhs) < TOL)


def demo_chain_rule(trials: int = 200) -> None:
    banner("5.  The chain rule: conditional readings from two ordinary tables")

    rng = random.Random(2718)
    xs = list(range(4))
    ys = list(range(3))
    zs = list(range(3))

    worst = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        p = random_population(len(xs), len(ys), len(zs), rng)
        pair_alphabet = [(y, z) for y in ys for z in zs]
        lhs = CMI(p, xs, ys, zs)
        rhs = MI(as_pair_table(p, xs, ys, zs), xs, pair_alphabet) - MI(
            marg_xz(p, xs, ys, zs), xs, zs
        )
        worst = max(worst, abs(lhs - rhs))

    print(f"  Over {trials} random weights, worst deviation in")
    print("      I(X;Y|Z) = I(X;(Y,Z)) - I(X;Z)")
    print(f"  is {worst:.3e}.")
    check("chain rule holds for arbitrary nonnegative weights", worst < 1e-8)

    xor = xor_population()
    pair_alphabet = [(y, z) for y in BOOLS for z in BOOLS]
    print("\n  On the XOR witness:")
    print(f"    I(X;(Y,Z)) = {MI(as_pair_table(xor, BOOLS, BOOLS, BOOLS), BOOLS, pair_alphabet):.6f}")
    print(f"    I(X;Z)     = {MI(marg_xz(xor, BOOLS, BOOLS, BOOLS), BOOLS, BOOLS):.6f}")
    print(f"    I(X;Y|Z)   = {CMI(xor, BOOLS, BOOLS, BOOLS):.6f}")


def demo_chaining(trials: int = 150) -> None:
    banner("6.  Chained merges: errors accumulate with a fixed sign")

    rng = random.Random(1618)
    xs = list(range(6))
    ys = list(range(3))
    zs = list(range(2))
    mid = list(range(4))
    out = list(range(2))

    worst_comp = 0.0
    worst_mono = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        p = random_population(len(xs), len(ys), len(zs), rng)
        tf = {x: rng.choice(mid) for x in xs}
        tg = {u: rng.choice(out) for u in mid}
        f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda x, t=tf: t[x]
        g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda u, t=tg: t[u]

        once = push_fst3(f, p, xs, ys, zs, mid)
        twice = push_fst3(g, once, mid, ys, zs, out)
        direct = push_fst3(lambda x, a=tf, b=tg: b[a[x]], p, xs, ys, zs, out)

        worst_comp = max(
            worst_comp, max(abs(twice[k] - direct[k]) for k in direct)
        )
        r_full = CMI(p, xs, ys, zs)
        r_once = CMI(once, mid, ys, zs)
        r_twice = CMI(twice, out, ys, zs)
        worst_mono = max(worst_mono, max(r_twice - r_once, r_once - r_full))

    print(f"  {trials} random pairs of merges.")
    print(f"  worst cell-wise discrepancy between chaining and composing: {worst_comp:.3e}")
    print(f"  worst violation of  I(g(f(X));Y|Z) <= I(f(X);Y|Z) <= I(X;Y|Z): {worst_mono:.3e}")
    check("merges compose", worst_comp < 1e-12)
    check("chained readings are monotone", worst_mono < TOL)


def demo_classification() -> None:
    banner("7.  Classification of invisible collisions")

    xs = [0, 1, 2]
    ys = [0, 1]
    zs = [0]
    us = [0, 1]
    merge: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda x: 0 if x in (0, 1) else 1

    def reading(p: Table3) -> Tuple[float, float]:
        return CMI(p, xs, ys, zs), CMI(push_fst3(merge, p, xs, ys, zs, us), us, ys, zs)

    # (a) the merged fiber {0,1} IS a product block: rows 0 and 1 are proportional
    prod: Table3 = {
        (0, 0, 0): 0.30, (0, 1, 0): 0.10,
        (1, 0, 0): 0.15, (1, 1, 0): 0.05,
        (2, 0, 0): 0.10, (2, 1, 0): 0.30,
    }
    prod = {(x, y, 0): prod.get((x, y, 0), 0.0) for x in xs for y in ys}
    t, m = reading(prod)
    print("  (a) fiber {0,1} is a product block (rows 3:1 and 3:1):")
    print(f"      true = {t:.6f}   merged = {m:.6f}   difference = {t - m:.3e}")
    check("product fiber => the collision is invisible", abs(t - m) < TOL)

    # (b) break proportionality in a single cell
    nonprod = dict(prod)
    nonprod[(1, 0, 0)] = 0.05
    nonprod[(1, 1, 0)] = 0.15
    t2, m2 = reading(nonprod)
    print("  (b) same merge, rows now 3:1 and 1:3 -- a single non-product cell:")
    print(f"      true = {t2:.6f}   merged = {m2:.6f}   drop = {t2 - m2:.6f} bits")
    check("non-product fiber => strict drop", t2 - m2 > TOL)
    print("  => a collision is invisible exactly when it merges dial settings with")
    print("     identical normalised response profiles in every context.")


def demo_context_merges() -> None:
    banner("8.  Why the guarantee lives on the dial axis only")

    xs = ys = zs = BOOLS
    collapse: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda _: True

    xor = xor_population()
    cop = copy_population()

    xor_before = CMI(xor, xs, ys, zs)
    xor_after = CMI(push_thd(collapse, xor, xs, ys, zs, [True]), xs, ys, [True])
    cop_before = CMI(cop, xs, ys, zs)
    cop_after = CMI(push_thd(collapse, cop, xs, ys, zs, [True]), xs, ys, [True])

    print(f"  XOR : merging contexts takes the reading {xor_before:.3f} -> {xor_after:.3f}  (drops)")
    print(f"  copy: merging contexts takes the reading {cop_before:.3f} -> {cop_after:.3f}  (rises)")
    check("context merges can lower the reading", xor_after < xor_before - TOL)
    check("context merges can raise the reading", cop_after > cop_before + TOL)
    print("  => on the context axis the error has no fixed sign; the one-sidedness")
    print("     theorem is genuinely about merges of the dial.")


def demo_capacity_cap(trials: int = 150) -> None:
    banner("9.  The capacity cap  I(X;Y|Z) <= H(X|Z)")

    rng = random.Random(4142)
    xs = list(range(4))
    ys = list(range(4))
    zs = list(range(2))

    worst = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        p = random_population(len(xs), len(ys), len(zs), rng)
        cap = 0.0
        for z in zs:
            s = slice_at(p, z)
            cap += entropy(marg1(s, xs, ys).values()) - nlp(mass(s))
        worst = max(worst, CMI(p, xs, ys, zs) - cap)
    print(f"  Over {trials} random weights, worst violation of the cap: {worst:.3e}")
    check("readings never exceed the surviving dial entropy", worst < TOL)


def main() -> None:
    print(__doc__)
    demo_witnesses()
    demo_one_sidedness()
    demo_exact_accounting()
    demo_error_bar()
    demo_chain_rule()
    demo_chaining()
    demo_classification()
    demo_context_merges()
    demo_capacity_cap()
    print()
    print("=" * 74)
    print("All checks passed.")
    print("=" * 74)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

demos.name: End-to-End Audit of a Coarsened Routing Table
demos.description: A realistic worked audit. Six routing rules are logged under only three identifiers, so the rules collide in pairs, and the table is read separately in three regions. The script plays both roles: it holds the true joint table, which a real auditor would not have, and the merged table, which is all the auditor sees. It first computes, from observables alone -- the merged table plus the per-region histogram of true rule counts -- the reading, the label-entropy error bar, the resulting bracket, and a verdict for each region (certified dependent, certified exact, or inconclusive with a stated budget of possibly hidden bits). It then reveals the truth and confirms that every verdict was sound and every bracket contained the true value. Next it localises the entire discrepancy to specific (region, colliding pair) cells and confirms that the local terms sum exactly to the loss. Finally it cross-checks all readings through the chain rule, an independent computational route. The scenario is constructed so that one collision is invisible because the pooled rules are conditionally exchangeable in that region, and another is invisible because one of the pooled rules is not deployed there -- two distinct routes to exactness without injectivity.
demos.code:
"""
An end-to-end audit of a coarsened routing table.

Scenario.  A system exposes 6 routing rules.  A downstream logger keeps only a
3-value identifier, so rules collide in pairs.  We hold the true table (which the
auditor would not have) and the merged table (which is all the auditor sees), and
run the full audit:

  1. compute the reading the auditor sees;
  2. compute the observable error bar from the encoding and the per-context dial
     histograms alone -- no access to the true joint table;
  3. issue a verdict for every context: certified dependent, certified exact, or
     inconclusive with a stated budget of possibly-missing bits;
  4. reveal the true readings and confirm that every verdict was correct and every
     bracket contained the truth;
  5. localise the discrepancy to specific (context, fiber) pairs;
  6. cross-check the conditional readings through the chain rule
     I(X;Y|Z) = I(X;(Y,Z)) - I(X;Z), an independent computational route.

Self-contained; run with  python3 demo2.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Cell3 = Tuple[Hashable, Hashable, Hashable]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# functionals
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def nlp(w: float) -> float:
    return -w * math.log2(w) if w > 0.0 else 0.0


def entropy(values: Iterable[float]) -> float:
    return sum(nlp(v) for v in values)


def deficit(values: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    return entropy(values) - nlp(sum(values))


def slice_reading(
    p: Dict[Cell3, float],
    dials: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    z: Hashable,
) -> float:
    rows = [[p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in responses] for x in dials]
    cells = [v for r in rows for v in r]
    cols = [sum(rows[i][j] for i in range(len(dials))) for j in range(len(responses))]
    return (entropy(sum(r) for r in rows) + entropy(cols)
            - entropy(cells) - nlp(sum(cells)))


def conditional_reading(
    p: Dict[Cell3, float],
    dials: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    contexts: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> float:
    return sum(slice_reading(p, dials, responses, z) for z in contexts)


def pair_reading(
    p: Dict[Cell3, float],
    dials: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    contexts: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> float:
    """I(X;(Y,Z)) -- the dial against the pair (response, context)."""
    cells = [[p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in responses for z in contexts] for x in dials]
    flat = [v for r in cells for v in r]
    cols = [sum(cells[i][j] for i in range(len(dials))) for j in range(len(cells[0]))]
    return entropy(sum(r) for r in cells) + entropy(cols) - entropy(flat)


def context_reading(
    p: Dict[Cell3, float],
    dials: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    contexts: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> float:
    """I(X;Z) -- the dial against the context, with the response summed out."""
    cells = [[sum(p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in responses) for z in contexts]
             for x in dials]
    flat = [v for r in cells for v in r]
    cols = [sum(cells[i][j] for i in range(len(dials))) for j in range(len(contexts))]
    return entropy(sum(r) for r in cells) + entropy(cols) - entropy(flat)


def merge_table(
    p: Dict[Cell3, float],
    f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    dials: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    contexts: Sequence[Hashable],
    labels: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> Dict[Cell3, float]:
    return {
        (u, y, z): sum(p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for x in dials if f(x) == u)
        for u in labels for y in responses for z in contexts
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the scenario
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

RULES = ["r0", "r1", "r2", "r3", "r4", "r5"]
OUTCOMES = ["hit", "miss"]
REGIONS = ["eu", "us", "ap"]
LABELS = ["L0", "L1", "L2"]

# the logger keeps only three identifiers
ENCODING = {"r0": "L0", "r1": "L0", "r2": "L1", "r3": "L1", "r4": "L2", "r5": "L2"}
encode: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable] = lambda r: ENCODING[r]

# The true population.  In 'eu' the colliding pair (r0, r1) is conditionally
# exchangeable (identical hit rates) so the collision there is invisible; in 'us'
# it is not; in 'ap' rule r1 never fires at all, so the collision is inactive.
TRUE: Dict[Cell3, float] = {}


def _fill() -> None:
    rows = {
        ("eu", "r0"): (0.09, 0.03),   # hit rate 0.75
        ("eu", "r1"): (0.06, 0.02),   # hit rate 0.75  -> exchangeable with r0
        ("eu", "r2"): (0.02, 0.08),
        ("eu", "r3"): (0.05, 0.05),
        ("eu", "r4"): (0.07, 0.03),
        ("eu", "r5"): (0.04, 0.06),
        ("us", "r0"): (0.10, 0.02),   # hit rate 0.83
        ("us", "r1"): (0.02, 0.10),   # hit rate 0.17  -> very different
        ("us", "r2"): (0.06, 0.04),
        ("us", "r3"): (0.03, 0.07),
        ("us", "r4"): (0.05, 0.05),
        ("us", "r5"): (0.08, 0.02),
        ("ap", "r0"): (0.12, 0.04),
        ("ap", "r1"): (0.00, 0.00),   # r1 is not deployed in ap
        ("ap", "r2"): (0.03, 0.09),
        ("ap", "r3"): (0.06, 0.06),
        ("ap", "r4"): (0.05, 0.03),
        ("ap", "r5"): (0.02, 0.10),
    }
    for (z, x), (hit, miss) in rows.items():
        TRUE[(x, "hit", z)] = hit
        TRUE[(x, "miss", z)] = miss


_fill()


def main() -> None:
    print(__doc__)
    merged = merge_table(TRUE, encode, RULES, OUTCOMES, REGIONS, LABELS)

    print("=" * 78)
    print("STEP 1-3.  What the auditor can compute (merged table + dial histograms)")
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"{'region':<8}{'merged':>10}{'error bar':>12}{'lower':>10}{'upper':>10}"
          f"   verdict")
    brackets: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]] = {}
    for z in REGIONS:
        m = slice_reading(merged, LABELS, OUTCOMES, z)
        hist = {x: sum(TRUE.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in OUTCOMES) for x in RULES}
        pooled: Dict[Hashable, float] = {u: 0.0 for u in LABELS}
        for x, w in hist.items():
            pooled[encode(x)] += w
        bar = entropy(hist.values()) - entropy(pooled.values())
        if m > 1e-12:
            verdict = "certified dependent"
        elif bar <= 1e-12:
            verdict = "certified exact"
        else:
            verdict = f"inconclusive (up to {bar:.4f} bits hidden)"
        brackets[z] = (m, m + bar)
        print(f"{z:<8}{m:>10.4f}{bar:>12.4f}{m:>10.4f}{m + bar:>10.4f}   {verdict}")

    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print("STEP 4.  Revealing the truth and checking every bracket")
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"{'region':<8}{'true':>10}{'bracket':>24}   contained?")
    for z in REGIONS:
        t = slice_reading(TRUE, RULES, OUTCOMES, z)
        lo, hi = brackets[z]
        ok = lo - 1e-9 <= t <= hi + 1e-9
        print(f"{z:<8}{t:>10.4f}     [{lo:.4f}, {hi:.4f}]        {'yes' if ok else 'NO'}")
        assert ok
    total_true = conditional_reading(TRUE, RULES, OUTCOMES, REGIONS)
    total_merged = conditional_reading(merged, LABELS, OUTCOMES, REGIONS)
    print(f"\n  totals:  true = {total_true:.4f} bits,  merged = {total_merged:.4f} bits,"
          f"  loss = {total_true - total_merged:.4f} bits")
    assert total_merged <= total_true + 1e-12

    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print("STEP 5.  Localising the loss to (region, colliding pair)")
    print("=" * 78)
    contributions: List[Tuple[str, str, float]] = []
    for z in REGIONS:
        row = {x: sum(TRUE.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in OUTCOMES) for x in RULES}
        for u in LABELS:
            fib = [x for x in RULES if encode(x) == u]
            d = (deficit([row[x] for x in fib])
                 - sum(deficit([TRUE.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for x in fib])
                       for y in OUTCOMES))
            contributions.append((z, u, d))
    contributions.sort(key=lambda t: -t[2])
    for z, u, d in contributions:
        pair = ", ".join(x for x in RULES if encode(x) == u)
        note = ""
        if d < 1e-9:
            note = "   <- invisible collision"
        print(f"  region {z:<4} label {u}  ({pair}) : {d:.6f} bits{note}")
    print(f"\n  sum of local terms = {sum(d for _, _, d in contributions):.6f} bits"
          f"   (equals the loss above)")
    assert abs(sum(d for _, _, d in contributions) - (total_true - total_merged)) < 1e-9

    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print("STEP 6.  Independent cross-check via the chain rule")
    print("=" * 78)
    for name, table, alphabet in (("true", TRUE, RULES), ("merged", merged, LABELS)):
        direct = conditional_reading(table, alphabet, OUTCOMES, REGIONS)
        via = (pair_reading(table, alphabet, OUTCOMES, REGIONS)
               - context_reading(table, alphabet, OUTCOMES, REGIONS))
        print(f"  {name:<7} direct = {direct:.6f}   "
              f"I(X;(Y,Z)) - I(X;Z) = {via:.6f}   agree: "
              f"{'yes' if abs(direct - via) < 1e-9 else 'NO'}")
        assert abs(direct - via) < 1e-9

    print()
    print("Audit complete: every verdict was sound and every bracket contained the truth.")
    print("The single largest contribution is the (us, L0) collision, which pools two")
    print("rules with hit rates 0.83 and 0.17.  The very same collision costs nothing in")
    print("'eu', where the two rules are conditionally exchangeable, and nothing in 'ap',")
    print("where one of them never fires -- exactness without injectivity, on both counts.")
    print("Note also how loose the observable error bar is here: it is a worst case over")
    print("all joint tables consistent with the dial histograms, and it is attained only")
    print("by extremal populations.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

algorithms.name: Slice-Wise Evaluation of the Conditional Reading
algorithms.description: The base computation on which everything else rests. Given an unnormalised nonnegative weight on dial x response x context, it evaluates I(X;Y|Z) in bits by summing, over contexts, the slice quantity H(row totals) + H(column totals) - H(cells) - nlp(slice mass). The final Shannon term is the mass correction that makes the definition valid for raw counts rather than probabilities: for a probability weight it vanishes because nlp(1) = 0, and the expression reduces to the textbook sum of p log2 (p(x,y,z)p(z) / (p(x,z)p(y,z))). Without the correction, slices whose mass differs from 1 would each be off by M log2 M and the total could even become negative. The routine performs a single pass over each slice, so it runs in O(|X||Y||Z|) time with O(|X||Y|) working space, which is optimal up to constants since every cell must be read.
algorithms.pseudocode:
function CONDITIONAL_READING(p, X, Y, Z):
    total <- 0
    for each context z in Z do
        for each x in X do  row[x] <- sum over y in Y of p(x,y,z)
        for each y in Y do  col[y] <- sum over x in X of p(x,y,z)
        mass <- sum over x in X of row[x]
        Hrow  <- sum over x of nlp(row[x])
        Hcol  <- sum over y of nlp(col[y])
        Hcell <- sum over (x,y) of nlp(p(x,y,z))
        total <- total + Hrow + Hcol - Hcell - nlp(mass)
    return total

where nlp(w) = -w * log2(w) for w > 0, and nlp(0) = 0.
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm A: slice-wise evaluation of the conditional reading."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Dict, Hashable, Iterable, Sequence, Tuple

Cell3 = Tuple[Hashable, Hashable, Hashable]


def nlp(w: float) -> float:
    """Shannon term -w log2 w, extended continuously by nlp(0) = 0."""
    return -w * math.log2(w) if w > 0.0 else 0.0


def entropy(values: Iterable[float]) -> float:
    """H(w) = sum of Shannon terms; no normalisation is assumed."""
    return sum(nlp(v) for v in values)


def conditional_reading(
    p: Dict[Cell3, float],
    dials: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    contexts: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> float:
    """Conditional mutual information I(X;Y|Z) in bits of an unnormalised weight.

    For every context z the slice reading is
        H(row totals) + H(column totals) - H(cells) - nlp(slice mass),
    and the conditional reading is the sum of those over contexts.  The final
    Shannon term is the mass correction that makes the definition valid for
    weights whose total mass is not 1 (raw counts, for instance).

    Complexity: O(|X| |Y| |Z|) time, O(|X| |Y|) working space.
    """
    total = 0.0
    for z in contexts:
        rows = [[p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in responses] for x in dials]
        row_totals = [sum(r) for r in rows]
        col_totals = [sum(rows[i][j] for i in range(len(dials)))
                      for j in range(len(responses))]
        cells = [v for r in rows for v in r]
        total += (entropy(row_totals) + entropy(col_totals)
                  - entropy(cells) - nlp(sum(cells)))
    return total

algorithms.name: Complete Attribution of a Collision Artifact to Context-Fiber Pairs
algorithms.description: Implements the exact accounting identity, which upgrades the data-processing inequality from a bound to a decomposition. For each context z and each fiber u of the merge it computes Delta(z,u), the deficit of the fiber's row totals minus the sum over responses of the deficits of its individual columns. Superadditivity of the deficit functional -- a consequence of the concavity of entropy -- makes each Delta nonnegative, and the identity guarantees that they sum exactly to the information the merge destroyed, with no residual left unexplained. This is what makes an artifact diagnosable rather than merely bounded: a discrepancy is never a diffuse defect of the table but is attributable to specific pairs, which the routine returns sorted by contribution so the dominant culprits appear first. A single strictly positive term is by itself a certificate that the merged reading is strictly below the truth. Cost is one pass per context over the joint table, O(|X||Y||Z|) time.
algorithms.pseudocode:
function LOCALISE_ARTIFACT(p, f, X, Y, Z, X'):
    for each label u in X' do  fiber[u] <- { x in X : f(x) = u }
    total <- 0 ;  contributions <- empty list
    for each context z in Z do
        for each x in X do  row[x] <- sum over y in Y of p(x,y,z)
        for each label u in X' do
            if fiber[u] is empty then continue
            pooled <- D( { row[x] : x in fiber[u] } )
            sliced <- 0
            for each y in Y do
                sliced <- sliced + D( { p(x,y,z) : x in fiber[u] } )
            delta <- pooled - sliced          // provably >= 0
            total <- total + delta
            append (z, u, delta) to contributions
    sort contributions by delta, descending
    return (total, contributions)

where D(S) = sum over v in S of nlp(v)  -  nlp(sum of S)
is the fiber deficit: the entropy destroyed by pooling the block S.
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm B: complete attribution of a collision artifact to (context, fiber) pairs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Cell3 = Tuple[Hashable, Hashable, Hashable]


def nlp(w: float) -> float:
    return -w * math.log2(w) if w > 0.0 else 0.0


def entropy(values: Iterable[float]) -> float:
    return sum(nlp(v) for v in values)


def deficit(values: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Fiber deficit D(S, w) = H(w|_S) - nlp(sum_S w): the entropy pooling destroys."""
    return entropy(values) - nlp(sum(values))


def localise_artifact(
    p: Dict[Cell3, float],
    f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    dials: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    contexts: Sequence[Hashable],
    labels: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> Tuple[float, List[Tuple[Hashable, Hashable, float]]]:
    """Attribute every lost bit to a (context, fiber) pair.

    Returns the total loss together with the list of local contributions

        Delta(z, u) = D(fiber u, dial marginal in context z)
                        - sum_y D(fiber u, response column y in context z),

    sorted by decreasing contribution.  Each term is nonnegative and the terms
    sum exactly to  I(X;Y|Z) - I(f(X);Y|Z),  so the attribution is complete: no
    residual is left unexplained.  A single strictly positive term is already a
    certificate that the merged reading is strictly below the truth.

    Complexity: O(|X| |Y| |Z|) time.
    """
    fibers: Dict[Hashable, List[Hashable]] = {
        u: [x for x in dials if f(x) == u] for u in labels
    }
    contributions: List[Tuple[Hashable, Hashable, float]] = []
    total = 0.0
    for z in contexts:
        marg = {x: sum(p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in responses) for x in dials}
        for u in labels:
            fib = fibers[u]
            if not fib:
                continue
            pooled = deficit([marg[x] for x in fib])
            sliced = sum(deficit([p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for x in fib])
                         for y in responses)
            d = pooled - sliced
            total += d
            contributions.append((z, u, d))
    contributions.sort(key=lambda t: -t[2])
    return total, contributions

algorithms.name: Audit Bracket from Observables Alone
algorithms.description: The operationally significant procedure, because it never touches the true joint table. Its inputs are the merged table the pipeline actually produced, the encoding, and the per-context histogram of true dial settings -- a marginal count an auditor genuinely has. From the histogram it computes the label entropy the merge destroys in each context, namely the entropy of the histogram minus the entropy of the pooled histogram. Theory then sandwiches the truth: the merged reading is a certified lower bound, and the merged reading plus the total label loss is a certified upper bound. Three verdicts follow mechanically. If the merged reading is positive the cell is certified dependent, since a merge can never inflate a reading. If no label entropy is destroyed anywhere then the reading is certified exact -- a strict generalisation of the injective case, requiring only that collisions be contextually inactive rather than globally absent. Otherwise the cell is inconclusive with an explicit budget of possibly missing bits. Cost is O(|X||Z| + |X'||Y||Z|), dominated by reading the merged table once.
algorithms.pseudocode:
function AUDIT_BRACKET(merged_table, dial_histograms, f, X', Y, Z):
    reading <- CONDITIONAL_READING(merged_table, X', Y, Z)
    bar <- 0
    for each context z in Z do
        hist <- dial_histograms[z]                 // marginal counts only
        pooled[u] <- 0 for every label u in X'
        for each dial setting x in hist do
            pooled[f(x)] <- pooled[f(x)] + hist[x]
        L[z] <- H(hist) - H(pooled)                // label entropy destroyed
        bar  <- bar + L[z]
    lower <- reading
    upper <- reading + bar
    if reading > 0 then verdict <- 'certified dependent'
    else if bar = 0 then verdict <- 'certified exact'
    else                 verdict <- 'inconclusive, up to bar bits hidden'
    return (lower, upper, L, verdict)
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm C: the audit bracket, computed without access to the true joint table."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Cell3 = Tuple[Hashable, Hashable, Hashable]


def nlp(w: float) -> float:
    return -w * math.log2(w) if w > 0.0 else 0.0


def entropy(values: Iterable[float]) -> float:
    return sum(nlp(v) for v in values)


def conditional_reading(
    p: Dict[Cell3, float],
    dials: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    contexts: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> float:
    total = 0.0
    for z in contexts:
        rows = [[p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in responses] for x in dials]
        cells = [v for r in rows for v in r]
        total += (entropy(sum(r) for r in rows)
                  + entropy(sum(rows[i][j] for i in range(len(dials)))
                            for j in range(len(responses)))
                  - entropy(cells) - nlp(sum(cells)))
    return total


def audit_bracket(
    merged_table: Dict[Cell3, float],
    dial_histograms: Dict[Hashable, Dict[Hashable, float]],
    f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    labels: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    contexts: Sequence[Hashable],
) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Bracket the true conditional reading using only observable quantities.

    Inputs are the *merged* table (what the pipeline actually produced), the
    per-context histogram of true dial settings (a marginal count, which an
    auditor does have), and the encoding f.  The true joint table is never used.

    The label entropy destroyed in a context is
        L(z) = H(dial histogram in z) - H(pooled histogram in z),
    a functional of the encoding and the marginal counts only.  The theory then
    guarantees
        merged reading  <=  true reading  <=  merged reading + sum_z L(z).

    The verdict is:
      * 'certified dependent'  -- the merged reading is positive, so the truth is;
      * 'certified exact'      -- no label entropy is destroyed anywhere, so the
                                  merged reading equals the truth even though the
                                  encoding may be far from injective;
      * 'inconclusive'         -- independence is reported, but up to the stated
                                  number of bits may have been destroyed.

    Complexity: O(|X||Z| + |X'||Y||Z|) time.
    """
    reading = conditional_reading(merged_table, labels, responses, contexts)

    label_loss_by_context: Dict[Hashable, float] = {}
    for z in contexts:
        hist = dial_histograms[z]
        pooled: Dict[Hashable, float] = {u: 0.0 for u in labels}
        for x, w in hist.items():
            pooled[f(x)] += w
        label_loss_by_context[z] = entropy(hist.values()) - entropy(pooled.values())

    bar = sum(label_loss_by_context.values())

    if reading > 1e-12:
        verdict = "certified dependent"
    elif bar <= 1e-12:
        verdict = "certified exact"
    else:
        verdict = "inconclusive"

    return {
        "merged_reading_bits": reading,
        "error_bar_bits": bar,
        "lower_bound_bits": reading,
        "upper_bound_bits": reading + bar,
        "label_loss_by_context": label_loss_by_context,
        "verdict": verdict,
    }

algorithms.name: Conditional-Exchangeability Certificate for a Label Merge
algorithms.description: Decides the classification criterion exactly. The merged reading equals the true one if and only if, in every context of positive mass, every fiber of the merge is a product block: each cell equals its row total times its column total divided by the fiber total. Equivalently, all dial settings pooled into one label share a single normalised response profile in that context, so they are conditionally exchangeable and no measurement of the response could have distinguished them. The routine tests every cell of every fiber in every context against its rank-one prediction, skipping fibers of zero mass, which are always exact. The output is a certificate in both directions: a global pass certifies that the merged reading is exactly the true one, and any single violated cell certifies that the reading is strictly below the truth. Violations are returned with their absolute deviations and sorted, so an engineer can see which contexts and pooled settings are responsible. Cost is O(|X||Y||Z|). Note the dichotomy is clean: there is no intermediate regime in which two sources of error cancel.
algorithms.pseudocode:
function EXCHANGEABILITY_CERTIFICATE(p, f, X, Y, Z, X', tol):
    for each label u in X' do  fiber[u] <- { x in X : f(x) = u }
    violations <- empty list
    for each context z in Z do
        for each x in X do  row[x] <- sum over y in Y of p(x,y,z)
        for each label u in X' do
            W <- sum over x in fiber[u] of row[x]
            if W <= tol then continue           // zero-mass fiber: always exact
            for each y in Y do
                col <- sum over x in fiber[u] of p(x,y,z)
                for each x in fiber[u] do
                    predicted <- row[x] * col / W       // rank-one prediction
                    if |p(x,y,z) - predicted| > tol then
                        append (z, u, x, y, p(x,y,z), predicted) to violations
    if violations is empty then
        return ('exact: the merge is invisible to the reading', [])
    else
        return ('strictly low: the merge is visible', violations sorted by deviation)
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm D: the conditional-exchangeability (product-block) certificate."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Cell3 = Tuple[Hashable, Hashable, Hashable]


def exchangeability_certificate(
    p: Dict[Cell3, float],
    f: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    dials: Sequence[Hashable],
    responses: Sequence[Hashable],
    contexts: Sequence[Hashable],
    labels: Sequence[Hashable],
    tol: float = 1e-9,
) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Decide whether a label merge is invisible to the conditional reading.

    The classification theorem states that the merged reading equals the true one
    if and only if, in every context of positive mass, every fiber of the merge is
    a product block:

        p_z(x, y) = row_total(x) * column_total(y) / fiber_total

    for all pooled settings x and all responses y.  Equivalently, all dial settings
    pooled into one label share a single normalised response profile in that
    context -- they are conditionally exchangeable, and no measurement of the
    response could have separated them.

    A single violated cell is a certificate that the reading is *strictly* low;
    a global pass is a certificate that the reading is exact.  The routine returns
    both the verdict and the list of violations with their absolute deviations,
    so an engineer can see which contexts and which pooled settings are at fault.

    Complexity: O(|X| |Y| |Z|) time.
    """
    fibers: Dict[Hashable, List[Hashable]] = {
        u: [x for x in dials if f(x) == u] for u in labels
    }
    violations: List[Dict[str, object]] = []

    for z in contexts:
        row = {x: sum(p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for y in responses) for x in dials}
        for u in labels:
            fib = fibers[u]
            total = sum(row[x] for x in fib)
            if total <= tol:
                continue                      # a fiber of zero mass is always exact
            for y in responses:
                col = sum(p.get((x, y, z), 0.0) for x in fib)
                for x in fib:
                    predicted = row[x] * col / total
                    actual = p.get((x, y, z), 0.0)
                    if abs(actual - predicted) > tol:
                        violations.append({
                            "context": z,
                            "label": u,
                            "dial": x,
                            "response": y,
                            "observed": actual,
                            "rank_one_prediction": predicted,
                            "deviation": abs(actual - predicted),
                        })

    violations.sort(key=lambda d: -float(d["deviation"]))
    return {
        "exact": len(violations) == 0,
        "verdict": ("merge is invisible: reading is exact"
                    if not violations else
                    "merge is visible: reading is strictly below the truth"),
        "violations": violations,
    }

visualizations.name: The One-Sided Cloud and the Audit Bracket
visualizations.description: Thousands of random three-way weight tables are each subjected to a random label merge, and the merged conditional reading is plotted against the true one. The entire cloud lies on or below the diagonal: the region above it is not sparsely populated but strictly empty, which is the data-processing inequality made visible. The companion histogram shows the loss expressed as a fraction of the observable error bar -- the label entropy the merge destroys, computable from the encoding and the marginal dial counts without any access to the true table. That fraction always lies in the unit interval, typically well inside it, with the upper endpoint attained by the extremal parity witness under a total collapse.
visualizations.code:
"""
Visualization: the one-sided cloud and the audit bracket.

For a few thousand random three-way weight tables and random label merges we plot
the merged conditional reading against the true one.  Two facts become visual:

  * every point lies weakly BELOW the diagonal -- no merge ever inflates a reading
    (the conditional data-processing inequality);
  * every point lies weakly ABOVE the shifted diagonal  y = x - L, where L is the
    label entropy the merge destroys -- an error bar computable from the encoding
    and the marginal dial counts alone, without any access to the true table.

The right-hand panel shows the distribution of the normalised loss  (true-merged)/L,
which lives in [0,1] and whose upper endpoint is attained.

Produces  one_sided_cloud.png.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, List, Sequence, Tuple

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def nlp(w: float) -> float:
    return -w * math.log2(w) if w > 0 else 0.0


def entropy(vals) -> float:
    return sum(nlp(v) for v in vals)


def cmi(p: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """p has shape (nx, ny, nz); returns the conditional reading in bits."""
    total = 0.0
    for z in range(p.shape[2]):
        s = p[:, :, z]
        total += (
            entropy(s.sum(axis=1))
            + entropy(s.sum(axis=0))
            - entropy(s.ravel())
            - nlp(s.sum())
        )
    return total


def merge(p: np.ndarray, code: Sequence[int], n_labels: int) -> np.ndarray:
    out = np.zeros((n_labels, p.shape[1], p.shape[2]))
    for x, u in enumerate(code):
        out[u] += p[x]
    return out


def label_loss(p: np.ndarray, code: Sequence[int], n_labels: int) -> float:
    total = 0.0
    for z in range(p.shape[2]):
        m1 = p[:, :, z].sum(axis=1)
        pooled = np.zeros(n_labels)
        for x, u in enumerate(code):
            pooled[u] += m1[x]
        total += entropy(m1) - entropy(pooled)
    return total


def main() -> None:
    rng = random.Random(20260908)
    npr = np.random.default_rng(20260908)

    nx, ny, nz, n_labels = 5, 3, 3, 2
    trials = 3000

    truths: List[float] = []
    merged: List[float] = []
    bars: List[float] = []

    for _ in range(trials):
        p = npr.random((nx, ny, nz))
        p *= npr.random((nx, ny, nz)) > 0.2          # random sparsity
        p /= max(p.sum(), 1e-12)                      # normalise for readability
        code = [rng.randrange(n_labels) for _ in range(nx)]
        t = cmi(p)
        m = cmi(merge(p, code, n_labels))
        L = label_loss(p, code, n_labels)
        truths.append(t)
        merged.append(m)
        bars.append(L)

    truths_a = np.array(truths)
    merged_a = np.array(merged)
    bars_a = np.array(bars)

    fig, (ax, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.6), width_ratios=[1.35, 1])

    ax.scatter(truths_a, merged_a, s=6, alpha=0.28, color="#2563eb",
               edgecolors="none", label="merged reading")
    lim = max(truths_a.max(), 0.01) * 1.05
    grid = np.linspace(0, lim, 200)
    ax.plot(grid, grid, color="#0f172a", lw=1.6, label="exactness line  $y=x$")
    ax.fill_between(grid, 0, grid, color="#22c55e", alpha=0.07)
    ax.text(lim * 0.55, lim * 0.90, "forbidden region\n(no merge ever lands here)",
            color="#b91c1c", fontsize=11, ha="center", style="italic")
    ax.set_xlabel("true reading  $I(X;Y\\mid Z)$  (bits)")
    ax.set_ylabel("merged reading  $I(f(X);Y\\mid Z)$  (bits)")
    ax.set_title("Every merge lands on or below the diagonal", fontsize=13)
    ax.set_xlim(0, lim)
    ax.set_ylim(0, lim)
    ax.legend(loc="lower right", frameon=False)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.15)

    ratio = np.where(bars_a > 1e-9, (truths_a - merged_a) / np.maximum(bars_a, 1e-12), np.nan)
    ratio = ratio[~np.isnan(ratio)]
    ax2.hist(ratio, bins=60, color="#f59e0b", alpha=0.85, edgecolor="none")
    ax2.axvline(0.0, color="#0f172a", lw=1.4)
    ax2.axvline(1.0, color="#b91c1c", lw=1.8)
    ax2.text(1.0, ax2.get_ylim()[1] * 0.92, "  bound attained\n  (collapse of the\n  parity witness)",
             color="#b91c1c", fontsize=10, va="top")
    ax2.set_xlim(-0.05, 1.15)
    ax2.set_xlabel("loss as a fraction of the observable error bar")
    ax2.set_ylabel("count")
    ax2.set_title("The bracket $0 \\leq \\mathrm{loss} \\leq$ label entropy destroyed",
                  fontsize=13)
    ax2.grid(alpha=0.15)

    fig.suptitle("One-sidedness of conditional-independence artifacts",
                 fontsize=15, y=0.99)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("one_sided_cloud.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote one_sided_cloud.png")
    print(f"maximum observed  merged - true  =  {float((merged_a - truths_a).max()):.3e}"
          "   (must be <= 0)")
    print(f"maximum observed  loss / bar     =  {float(ratio.max()):.6f}   (must be <= 1)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.name: Artifact Localisation and Monotone Decay Along a Chain
visualizations.description: Two panels. The left displays, for one concrete table and merge, the matrix of local contributions to the loss, one entry per (context, fiber) pair. Each entry is nonnegative and the matrix sums exactly to the information destroyed, so the attribution is complete: every lost bit has a return address. The right panel follows a chain of successive coarsenings from eight labels down to one. Because merges compose -- applying one merge after another is the same as applying the composite -- the guarantee reapplies at each stage and the readings decay monotonically; the capacity cap given by the surviving conditional dial entropy is shown alongside, always dominating the reading and collapsing to zero along with it.
visualizations.code:
"""
Visualization: localisation of the artifact, and monotone decay along a chain.

Left panel.  For one concrete table and one concrete merge we display the matrix
of local contributions

    Delta(z, u) = D(fiber u, dial marginal in context z)
                    - sum_y D(fiber u, column y in context z),

each entry nonnegative, the whole matrix summing exactly to the information the
merge destroyed.  This is what makes an artifact diagnosable: every lost bit has
a return address, namely a (context, fiber) pair.

Right panel.  A chain of successive merges 8 -> 6 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 labels.
Because merges compose -- applying g after f is the same as applying g o f --
the guarantee reapplies at every stage and the readings decay monotonically.
Errors accumulate, but always with the same sign; a later defect can never undo
an earlier one and push the reading back above the truth.

Produces  localisation_and_chain.png.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def nlp(w: float) -> float:
    return -w * math.log2(w) if w > 0 else 0.0


def entropy(vals) -> float:
    return sum(nlp(v) for v in vals)


def deficit(vals: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    return entropy(vals) - nlp(sum(vals))


def cmi(p: np.ndarray) -> float:
    total = 0.0
    for z in range(p.shape[2]):
        s = p[:, :, z]
        total += (entropy(s.sum(axis=1)) + entropy(s.sum(axis=0))
                  - entropy(s.ravel()) - nlp(s.sum()))
    return total


def merge(p: np.ndarray, code: Sequence[int], n_labels: int) -> np.ndarray:
    out = np.zeros((n_labels, p.shape[1], p.shape[2]))
    for x, u in enumerate(code):
        out[u] += p[x]
    return out


def local_terms(p: np.ndarray, code: Sequence[int], n_labels: int) -> np.ndarray:
    nz = p.shape[2]
    out = np.zeros((nz, n_labels))
    for z in range(nz):
        s = p[:, :, z]
        m1 = s.sum(axis=1)
        for u in range(n_labels):
            fib = [x for x in range(p.shape[0]) if code[x] == u]
            if not fib:
                continue
            marg = deficit([m1[x] for x in fib])
            sliced = sum(deficit([s[x, y] for x in fib]) for y in range(p.shape[1]))
            out[z, u] = marg - sliced
    return out


def main() -> None:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)

    # ---------------- left panel: localisation ----------------
    nx, ny, nz, n_labels = 8, 4, 5, 3
    p = rng.random((nx, ny, nz)) * (rng.random((nx, ny, nz)) > 0.25)
    p /= p.sum()
    code = [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2]

    loss = cmi(p) - cmi(merge(p, code, n_labels))
    terms = local_terms(p, code, n_labels)

    fig, (ax, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13.5, 5.4), width_ratios=[1.1, 1])

    im = ax.imshow(terms, cmap="magma", aspect="auto")
    for z in range(nz):
        for u in range(n_labels):
            ax.text(u, z, f"{terms[z, u]:.3f}", ha="center", va="center",
                    color="white" if terms[z, u] < terms.max() * 0.6 else "black",
                    fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xticks(range(n_labels))
    ax.set_xticklabels([f"fiber {u}\n{{{','.join('x'+str(x) for x in range(nx) if code[x]==u)}}}"
                        for u in range(n_labels)], fontsize=9)
    ax.set_yticks(range(nz))
    ax.set_yticklabels([f"context $z_{z}$" for z in range(nz)])
    ax.set_title(f"Where the {loss:.4f} lost bits came from\n"
                 f"(entries sum to {terms.sum():.4f})", fontsize=12)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="bits of loss attributable to this (context, fiber)")

    # ---------------- right panel: chain ----------------
    nx2, ny2, nz2 = 8, 4, 3
    q = rng.random((nx2, ny2, nz2)) * (rng.random((nx2, ny2, nz2)) > 0.15)
    q /= q.sum()

    stages: List[Tuple[str, Sequence[int], int]] = [
        ("8 labels\n(identity)",  [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], 8),
        ("6 labels",              [0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5], 6),
        ("4 labels",              [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3], 4),
        ("3 labels",              [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2], 3),
        ("2 labels",              [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1], 2),
        ("1 label\n(collapse)",   [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], 1),
    ]
    readings = [cmi(merge(q, code, k)) for _, code, k in stages]
    caps = []
    for _, code, k in stages:
        cap = 0.0
        m = merge(q, code, k)
        for z in range(nz2):
            s = m[:, :, z]
            cap += entropy(s.sum(axis=1)) - nlp(s.sum())
        caps.append(cap)

    xs = np.arange(len(stages))
    ax2.plot(xs, caps, "o--", color="#94a3b8", lw=1.6, ms=6,
             label="capacity cap  $H(X\\mid Z)$ after the merge")
    ax2.plot(xs, readings, "o-", color="#2563eb", lw=2.4, ms=9,
             label="conditional reading  $I(f(X);Y\\mid Z)$")
    ax2.fill_between(xs, readings, caps, color="#94a3b8", alpha=0.12)
    for i, r in enumerate(readings):
        ax2.annotate(f"{r:.3f}", (xs[i], r), textcoords="offset points",
                     xytext=(0, 12), ha="center", fontsize=9, color="#1e3a8a")
    ax2.set_xticks(xs)
    ax2.set_xticklabels([s[0] for s in stages], fontsize=9)
    ax2.set_ylabel("bits")
    ax2.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    ax2.set_title("A chain of merges: readings decay, and never recover", fontsize=12)
    ax2.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=10)
    ax2.grid(alpha=0.15)

    fig.suptitle("Exact accounting and chained coarsening", fontsize=15, y=0.995)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("localisation_and_chain.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote localisation_and_chain.png")
    print(f"loss = {loss:.6f} bits;  sum of local terms = {terms.sum():.6f} bits")
    print("readings along the chain:", " >= ".join(f"{r:.4f}" for r in readings))
    assert all(readings[i] >= readings[i + 1] - 1e-9 for i in range(len(readings) - 1))
    assert all(readings[i] <= caps[i] + 1e-9 for i in range(len(readings)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.name: The Dichotomy of Invisible Collisions
visualizations.description: A merge pools two dial settings within one context. Their normalised response profiles are slid apart from identical to maximally different, and the information destroyed is plotted against the separation. The curve touches zero at exactly one point -- where the pooled block becomes a product block -- and is strictly positive on both sides, for every split of the fiber's mass between the two settings. There is no interval of near-misses in which two sources of error accidentally cancel. The second panel sweeps both the profile separation and the mass split simultaneously, exhibiting the zero set as the single line where the profiles agree, which is exactly the classification theorem drawn as a picture.
visualizations.code:
"""
Visualization: the dichotomy of invisible collisions.

A merge pools two dial settings inside one context.  We slide their normalised
response profiles apart, from identical (a product block) to maximally different,
and watch the information the merge destroys.

The classification theorem says the loss vanishes *exactly* at the point where
the two profiles coincide, and is strictly positive everywhere else -- there is
no interval of near-misses in which two sources of error accidentally cancel.
The plot shows precisely that: a single tangential zero at the product point, and
strict positivity on both sides.

The second panel varies the mass balance inside the fiber, showing that the
zero set is exactly the one-dimensional family of product blocks regardless of
how the fiber's weight is split between the two pooled settings.

Produces  dichotomy.png.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def nlp(w: float) -> float:
    return -w * math.log2(w) if w > 0 else 0.0


def entropy(vals) -> float:
    return sum(nlp(v) for v in vals)


def reading(rows: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Single-context conditional reading of a (dial x response) block."""
    return (entropy(rows.sum(axis=1)) + entropy(rows.sum(axis=0))
            - entropy(rows.ravel()) - nlp(rows.sum()))


def loss_for(theta: float, alpha: float, base_profile: float = 0.5) -> float:
    """Two pooled settings with profiles (base +- theta), plus one untouched setting.

    alpha is the share of the fiber's mass carried by the first setting.
    Returns the information destroyed by pooling the first two rows.
    """
    W = 0.6                       # mass of the fiber
    pa, pb = base_profile + theta, base_profile - theta
    rows = np.array([
        [alpha * W * pa,       alpha * W * (1 - pa)],
        [(1 - alpha) * W * pb, (1 - alpha) * W * (1 - pb)],
        [0.10,                 0.30],                       # a third, unmerged setting
    ])
    merged = np.array([rows[0] + rows[1], rows[2]])
    return reading(rows) - reading(merged)


def main() -> None:
    thetas = np.linspace(-0.45, 0.45, 601)

    fig, (ax, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.2))

    for alpha, colour in [(0.5, "#2563eb"), (0.3, "#059669"), (0.15, "#b45309")]:
        losses = [loss_for(t, alpha) for t in thetas]
        ax.plot(thetas, losses, lw=2.2, color=colour,
                label=f"fiber mass split {alpha:.2f} / {1-alpha:.2f}")
    ax.axvline(0.0, color="#0f172a", lw=1.3, ls=":")
    ax.axhline(0.0, color="#0f172a", lw=1.0)
    ax.annotate("profiles coincide:\nthe collision is invisible",
                xy=(0, 0), xytext=(0.13, 0.055), fontsize=10, color="#0f172a",
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#0f172a", lw=1.2))
    ax.set_xlabel("profile separation  $\\theta$   (response probabilities $0.5\\pm\\theta$)")
    ax.set_ylabel("information destroyed by the merge (bits)")
    ax.set_title("Zero loss occurs at exactly one point, not on an interval", fontsize=12)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=10)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.15)
    ax.set_ylim(bottom=-0.005)

    # panel 2: heat map over (theta, alpha)
    alphas = np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 200)
    grid = np.array([[loss_for(t, a) for t in thetas[::4]] for a in alphas])
    im = ax2.imshow(grid, origin="lower", aspect="auto", cmap="viridis",
                    extent=[thetas[0], thetas[-1], alphas[0], alphas[-1]])
    ax2.contour(thetas[::4], alphas, grid, levels=[1e-6], colors="white", linewidths=2)
    ax2.set_xlabel("profile separation  $\\theta$")
    ax2.set_ylabel("share of fiber mass on the first setting")
    ax2.set_title("The zero set is the single line $\\theta = 0$", fontsize=12)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax2, label="bits destroyed")

    fig.suptitle("Classification of invisible collisions: a clean dichotomy",
                 fontsize=15, y=0.99)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("dichotomy.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote dichotomy.png")
    print(f"loss at theta = 0      : {loss_for(0.0, 0.5):.3e}  (must be 0)")
    print(f"loss at theta = 0.01   : {loss_for(0.01, 0.5):.3e}  (must be > 0)")
    print(f"loss at theta = -0.01  : {loss_for(-0.01, 0.5):.3e}  (must be > 0)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

interactive_demos.title: The Collision Laboratory
interactive_demos.description: A live workbench for the whole theory on a three-dial, two-response, two-context table. Every cell of the true joint table is editable and every quantity recomputes instantly: the true conditional reading, the reading you would see off the merged table, the information destroyed, and the observable error bar. A horizontal bracket shows the certified region in which the truth must lie, and a verdict panel classifies the reading as certified dependent, a false negative, or genuinely null. Below, a live heat map displays the exact per-(context, fiber) accounting: each entry nonnegative, the entries summing precisely to the loss, so the user can watch a discrepancy being attributed to specific cells rather than merely bounded. A running exchangeability test reports whether every fiber is a product block and, if not, names the offending cells. Four presets teach the four key phenomena: the parity witness under total collapse, where a full bit of genuine dependence is reported as zero; an exchangeable fiber, where a collision is completely invisible; a context-disjoint collision, where a wildly non-injective encoding is nevertheless exact; and randomisation, which invites the user to try -- and fail -- to push the merged reading above the true one.
interactive_demos.html:
The Collision Laboratory

Edit the true joint table below. Three dial settings x₀, x₁, x₂, two responses y₀, y₁, two contexts z₀, z₁. Then choose which dial settings a faulty encoding pools together. Everything on the right recomputes live: the true conditional reading, the reading you would see off the merged table, the exact per-(context, fiber) accounting of every lost bit, and the error bar an auditor could compute without ever seeing this table. Watch two things: the merged reading never rises above the true one, and it stops dropping exactly when the pooled rows become proportional.

The true table

Encoding  
The exchangeable fiber preset makes rows x₀ and x₁ proportional in both contexts — the collision then becomes completely invisible. The context-disjoint preset lets x₀ fire only in z₀ and x₁ only in z₁: a wildly non-injective encoding that is nevertheless exact.

What the tables report

True conditional reading  I(X;Y|Z) —
Merged reading  I(f(X);Y|Z) —
Information destroyed —
Observable error bar (label entropy destroyed) —
what you measure certified upper region (reading + error bar)
Why the bar can only shrink — the one-line reason
Pooling a block of rows destroys entropy; call that the block's deficit. You can pool a fiber after summing over responses (the marginal deficit) or inside each response column and then add up (the sliced deficits). Concavity of entropy says the sliced version is always the smaller of the two, and the difference is exactly the information the merge destroyed. Nonnegative differences summed over contexts and fibers give a nonnegative total — that is the whole theorem.

Exact accounting: where each lost bit came from

The total loss is the sum of these cells, and every cell is nonnegative. A discrepancy is never a diffuse fog over the table — it is attributable to a specific (context, fiber) pair. A single positive cell already forces the whole merged reading strictly below the truth.

interactive_demos.description: An interactive demonstration of the exact boundary of the guarantee. On a two-by-two-by-two table the user compares two operations: collapsing the dial and collapsing the context. Both readings are plotted as movable points on a shared number line with arrows showing the direction each operation pushes the value. Collapsing the dial always moves left, never right -- that is the theorem. Collapsing the context moves either way: on the parity table, where the variables are independent overall but perfectly coupled inside each context, it destroys a full bit; on the copy table, where the variables are coupled overall but conditionally trivial, it manufactures a full bit of dependence that is simply not there. Those same two tables also prove that the conditional and unconditional readings are logically independent, so no statement about single-dial tables follows from the conditional guarantee. An expandable panel explains the structural reason for the asymmetry: a dial merge operates inside a fixed context slice, where concavity of entropy pins the sign, while a context merge recombines slices, where nothing constrains the direction.
interactive_demos.html:
Two Axes, Two Fates

The one-sidedness guarantee is not a general fact about coarsening. It lives on the dial axis only. Pool dial settings and the reading can only fall. Pool contexts and the reading can fall or rise — it can manufacture a dependence from nothing. Both effects are on display below on a two-by-two-by-two table you can edit.

The table (weights on x, y, z)

On the parity table the two variables are independent overall but perfectly coupled in each context. On the copy table it is the reverse: strongly coupled overall, nothing left once the context is known.

Readings on a number line (bits)

true reading I(X;Y|Z) after collapsing the dial after collapsing the context
Why do the two axes behave differently? (click to expand)

The exact accounting identity explains it. A dial merge replaces, inside a fixed context slice, the marginal deficit of a pooled block by the sum of its per-response sliced deficits. Concavity of entropy says the sliced version is always the smaller, so the difference — the loss — is always nonnegative. The arithmetic happens entirely within one slice, and a convexity argument pins the sign.

A context merge does something structurally different: it recombines slices, replacing several separate slice readings by the single reading of their sum. Nothing constrains the direction of that recombination. Two slices in which the dial and response are coupled in opposite ways can cancel when added, destroying dependence; two slices that are individually structureless can, when added, create an apparent association — the mechanism behind Simpson-style reversals. So: everything one-sided in this theory happens on the dial axis, everything two-sided on the context axis.

The practical consequence is sharp. If your pipeline coarsens the explanatory variable, every reported dependence is real. If it coarsens the conditioning variable — pooling regions, bucketing hours, aggregating cohorts — nothing at all is guaranteed and each reading needs its own argument.
